c.tagline: Sun-soaked gateway to the Black Forest, a Gothic university city built on solar energy and easygoing charm.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis use standardized metered fares set by the local tariff board; ranks are common at the station and old town, and phone/app booking is typical.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide number for fire and medical emergencies and also reaches police; 110 is the direct German police line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Mind fast bike traffic and the Bächle street channels; minor petty theft around the Hauptbahnhof late at night.

hood_desc: The compact medieval old town around Freiburg Minster, laced with trickling Bächle water runnels; the obvious base for first-time visitors with everything walkable.
A pioneering car-reduced eco-district of solar homes and the famous Solar Settlement, built on a former French military base; popular with sustainability-minded travelers and families.
An elegant, leafy residential quarter of Belle Epoque villas south of the center, home to the Colombischlössle museum and a relaxed cafe scene; suits travelers wanting a quieter, upscale base.
A mixed residential and student district near the main train station, with affordable eateries and a multicultural feel; convenient for arrivals by rail.
A quiet hillside neighborhood below the Schlossberg with vineyard paths and views over the city; good for travelers who want nature and calm close to downtown.

water.note: Tap water is excellent and safe to drink.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 4:30 AM to around 1:00 AM, with a weekend Nachtbus night network on Friday and Saturday nights.
transit.pay: Tickets from the RVF regional fare network cover trams and buses; buy from machines, the VAG/Freiburg app, or as a rechargeable card, with contactless bank card tap-in increasingly common.
transit.note: Freiburg's Stadtbahn tram network is one of the most extensive per capita in Germany and, together with an extensive bike-path network, makes a car largely unnecessary in the city.

air: Frankfurt Airport (FRA, ~220 km via ICE train)

transit.m: Airport bus/shuttle to Freiburg Hauptbahnhof (~50 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory since service is included, but rounding up or adding roughly 5-10% for good service is customary; tips are usually handed directly to the server rather than left on the table.

landmarks: Freiburg Münster (Minster)
A Gothic masterpiece with a filigree 116-meter openwork spire, praised as the most beautiful tower in Christendom, that survived wartime bombing intact.
Münsterplatz and the Münstermarkt
The cathedral square's beloved daily market, where farmers sell Black Forest produce and stalls sizzle with the city's famous lange Rote sausages.
The Bächle
Freiburg's medieval network of narrow water channels babbling along the old town streets; legend says stepping in one destines you to marry a local.
Schlossberg and Tower
The forested hill rising straight from the old town, its spiral lookout tower rewarding a short climb with views to the Vosges.
Schauinsland Cable Car
One of Germany's longest cableways, floating 3.6 kilometers up a 1,284-meter Black Forest summit for hiking trails and panoramas of the Alps.
Historisches Kaufhaus
The arcaded crimson merchants' hall of 1530 on Münsterplatz, adorned with statues of Habsburg emperors and glittering oriel turrets.
Martinstor
The older of Freiburg's two surviving medieval city gates, a 13th-century tower now standing photogenically astride the tram lines.
Schwabentor
The picture-book second medieval gate with its painted facade and small local history exhibits, marking the old road toward Swabia.
Augustinermuseum
A former monastery turned superb art museum, presenting medieval sculpture, original Münster stained glass and Baden masterpieces on an elegant walkway circuit.
Rathausplatz and the New Town Hall
A chestnut-shaded square of Renaissance facades and carillon chimes, fronted by the twin-gabled town halls and the Franciscan church of St. Martin.

train.note: Everything leaves from Freiburg Hauptbahnhof, five minutes' walk west of the Altstadt across the Stadtbahnbrucke. Basel is only about 45 minutes away and Zurich around 2h, which makes Freiburg an easy Swiss gateway - remember that Basel Badischer Bahnhof stands on German soil, so you clear Swiss customs there or at Basel SBB. One TGV inOui pair a day runs to Strasbourg and Paris Est in roughly 3h30, and OeBB Nightjet sleepers pass through overnight towards Zurich, Amsterdam, Berlin and Hamburg. The old cross-border railway to Colmar is still severed west of Breisach, so France is reached by bus, or by train via Basel or Strasbourg.

intl.to: Strasbourg & Colmar (France), Basel & Zurich (Switzerland), Milan (Italy) & across Europe

bus.note: Long-distance coaches use the ZOB on the west side of Freiburg Hauptbahnhof, reached over the Stadtbahnbrucke footbridge above the platforms. Tickets are bought online; there is no staffed counter. Basel is about an hour by coach, Strasbourg roughly 1h30 and Munich around 5h. Regional buses of the SudbadenBus and RVF network cover the Black Forest, the Kaiserstuhl and Breisach on the Rhine.

ferry.note: Freiburg lies inland at the western edge of the Black Forest and its river, the Dreisam, is a shallow mountain stream, so there are no ferries or passenger boats. The nearest boat traffic is on the Rhine at Breisach, about 25 km west, where river-cruise ships call, and the nearest scheduled lake shipping is on Lake Constance roughly two hours away.

half.name: Titisee
half.blurb: Glacial lake in the heart of the Black Forest, ringed by pine forest and famous for its cuckoo-clock shops.

half.name: Colmar
half.blurb: Alsatian town of half-timbered houses and canals just across the French border, often called Little Venice.

half.name: Basel
half.blurb: Swiss city on the Rhine with a red sandstone medieval Münster and one of Europe's leading modern art museums.

half.name: Triberg Waterfalls
half.blurb: One of Germany's highest waterfalls, cascading in stages through a forested gorge in the Black Forest.
